prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the geometry of an indoor living room with no other people present, showing an arched ceiling entrance and a near foreground table/stool (<1 m) in Frame 1, a central wooden coffee table (~1.5–2.5 m ahead) flanked by a TV stand on the left (~2 m) and a couch on the right (~2–3 m) spaced about 1.5–2 m apart, and two armchairs with bookcases and a window in the far background (~3.5–4.5 m). Across the 5 frames, the camera wearer pitches their head sharply downward and moves forward toward the floor and coffee table, bringing the near edge of the coffee table and a small foreground stool with a furry cover from roughly 1.5–2 m away into immediate arm's reach (<0.5–1 m) in Frames 4 and 5 while the background furniture moves out of the upper field of view. It clearly reveals the 3D planar slant of the floor, the vertical relief of the dark couch cushions and shadowed left-side console that blend into darkness in the RGB image, and the sharp depth discontinuity between the foreground stool, the coffee table, and the rug beneath them. However, the map looks unreliable around the bright window and lamp between the far bookcases in Frames 1–2 where glare flattens depth into a uniform black void, and in Frame 5 where extreme close-up motion blur causes the foreground rug and stool surfaces to bleed together without crisp boundaries.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map detects only a sparse subset of the room's furniture across the first three frames and completely fails to segment the central wooden coffee table, bookcases, lamps, or floor in any frame. In Frame 1, it labels the distant left armchair (~3.5 m), the right-side couch (~2.5 m, positioned ~1.5 m right of the center table), and a near bottom-right chair (~1.5 m, partly cut off at the frame edge), while in Frame 2 it picks up the left-wall TV (~1.8 m, partly out of view on the upper left), both distant armchairs (~3–3.5 m, spaced ~1 m apart and facing roughly toward the camera wearer's area), and the right couch (~2 m) as the wearer approaches and tilts downward. By Frame 3, as the camera pitches further down toward the coffee table (~1–1.5 m away, entering arm's reach), all furniture masks vanish and the wooden coffee table is falsely segmented as a 'person' in the center of the frame, followed by zero detections in Frames 4 and 5 when only the close-up table edge, dark rug, and foreground stool (<0.5–1 m) remain in view. While the masks in Frames 1 and 2 help isolate the boundaries of the dark couch and shadowed armchairs that are dim in the RGB strip, the map is highly unreliable overall—misclassifying a cardboard box resting on the left armchair in Frame 2 as a 'tv', hallucinating the coffee table as a 'person' in Frame 3, and missing all close-range objects in Frames 4–5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map confirms that no standing or seated people are facing or looking toward the camera wearer in the room, showing almost entirely black frames across the sequence as the wearer walks forward and looks down at the coffee table and floor. Its only detection appears in Frame 1 at the bottom-left (~2.5–3 m from the camera wearer, below and to the left of the central coffee table), where a small cluster of yellow body keypoints is erroneously plotted on a decorative patterned object/plant stand near the left armchair. Across Frames 2 through 5, as the camera wearer tilts their head down and brings the coffee table and furry foreground stool within arm's reach (<0.5–1 m), no body or hand skeletons (yellow or magenta) are detected, confirming that neither the camera wearer's own hands nor any other person's limbs enter the field of view. Rather than adding spatial insight beyond the RGB image, this map is unreliable in Frame 1 due to its false-positive skeleton hallucination on inanimate clutter in the dim lower-left corner, though it accurately reflects the absence of visible human bodies or hands in Frames 2–5.
